string.comment: Each value is a time with unit. %1$s=whole training, %2$s=linear part, %3$s=small network, %4$s=GRU of the expected curve, %5$s=measuring on the test days. Example: Training took 9 min: linear part 4 s, network 25 s, expected curve 8 min, measuring 12 s

string.comment: %1$d=percent. Example: All moments of the test days. AutoISF only on its 3 % of them, too few to compare.

resources.string: All moments of the test days. AutoISF only on its %1$d %% of them, too few to compare.

string.name: learned_row_cgm_only
string.comment: Row of a table: the error of a simple yardstick that reads only BG, no insulin and no carbs

string.name: learned_versus_autoisf
string.comment: %1$s=list of curves, each with its 60-minute error minus that of AutoISF and the 95 % range over the test days. Example: 60 min error minus AutoISF, 95 % range over the days: GRU -6 mg/dl (-9 mg/dl … -3 mg/dl), Linear +2 mg/dl (-1 mg/dl … +5 mg/dl). A range that holds 0 is not sure.

resources.string: 60 min error minus AutoISF, 95 %% range over the days: %1$s. A range that holds 0 is not sure.

string.name: learned_lows_seen
string.comment: %1$s=BG with units, %2$d=number of lows, %3$s=list of curves, each with the lows it saw coming and in brackets its false warnings. Example: Lows below 70 mg/dl at 30 or 60 min: 25. Seen coming (false warnings): GRU 18 (4), Linear 15 (6), AutoISF 14 (9)

resources.string: Lows below %1$s at 30 or 60 min: %2$d. Seen coming (false warnings): %3$s

string.name: learned_row_naive
string.comment: Row of a table: the error of a guess that BG does not change
